The Police Sub-Inspector of Sanjay Nagara Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused
No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable under Section 498(A), 323, 504, 506 read with sec.34 of Indian
Pen
al Code and Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act

. 
2. Prosecution Case:

The marriage of CW1 Smt. Tanzeem Banu and accused No.1 was solemnized on 16-04-2022 as per Muslim customs demanded and received Rs.2 lakhs, gold ring from CW2 Sri Sradhar Pasha as dowry and thereafter they were residing at No.18, 3rd Cross, Bhoopasandra,
Jamiya Masjid within the limits of Sanjayanagara PS.
Thereafter, the accused No.1 to 3 with common intention started ill-treating CW1 and subjected her to mental and physical cruelty by demanding additional dowry.
In the year 2019, when CW1 came to know about the illicit relationship of accused No.1 with one Nageena i.e. accused No.4.
When the CW1 questioned the relationship, the accused threatened to kill her if she told the family.

In the month of November 2020, accused No. 1 to 3 insisted CW1 to purchase one car from her parents and for that CW2 and CW3 purchased the Tata Punch KA 04M Z8614 car in the name of CW1 and given to accused No.1.

On 17-05-2022, the quarrel held between CW1 and accused persons in respect of illicit relationship between accused No.1 and 4, at that time the accused No.1 to 3 with common intention harassed CW1 to fetch Rs.5 lakhs as additional dowry from her parental house and thrown her out of the house.

On 28-05-2022, when CW1 to CW5 came to house of accused to sort out the differences, the accused No.1 to 3 with common intention picked up quarrel with CW1, demanded for Rs.5 lakhs and accused No.1 abused CW1 with filthy language and beaten Tanzeem Banu vs Fiyaz Pasha on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166094722/

her with hands thereby accused persons subjected the CW1 to mental and physical cruelty.
3. First Information Report:

On the basis of first information given by informant cum CW1 namely Smt. Tanzeem Bani, the PSI of Sanjaynagara police registered a Crime No.121/2022 against the accused for the offenses punishable under Section 498(A), 504 and 506 of IPC and Sec.3, 4 of D.P.Act, prepared FIR and sent the same to the Court and to his superior officers.
4.
Investigation:

After registration of the case, CW13 Sri Subramani.M. PSI of Sanjaynagara Police Station drawn spot mahazar on 06-06-2022 and handed over the case papers to CW14 Sri Guruprasad PI of Sanjaynagara police station and KABC030074402023 CC No.4753/2023 recorded the requisite witnesses and collected the documents and submitted the charge sheet against accused No.1 to 4 for the offenses punishable under Section 498(A), 323, 504 and 506 read with sec.34 of IPC and Sec.3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
5. The accused No.1 to 4 were enlarged on bail by the order dated 03-02-2024.

6. On receipt of charge sheet, this Court took cognizance of offence alleged against the accused No.1 to 3.
7.

Copies of prosecution papers as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused No.1 to 4.
8.
Charge:

After hearing learned Sr.APP and counsel for accused, charge for the offences punishable U/Sec.498(A), 323, 504, 506 read with Sec.34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act has been framed, read over and explained to the accused in the language known to them, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
KABC030074402023 CC No.4753/2023 9. Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 14 witnesses however examined one witness and exhibited 3 documents.

The learned Sr.APP prayed for issuance of summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that the material witness has not supported the case and hence the prosecution side was taken as closed on 23-09-2024.

10. Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: There are no incriminating evidences against the accused persons from the evidence of prosecution thereby the recording of statement of accused as per Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with.
11. Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

She further stated that when she went to police station for settlement of minor differences of opinion amongst her and accused No.1, the police obtained her signatures on the said documents and she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P1 and 2.
In this regard, the learned Sr.APP has cross examined this witness by treating her as hostile witness but no favorable answer has been elicited from her mouth to support the prosecution case.

Her denial of statement given before the police is marked as Ex.P3.
15.

Though the prosecution has cross examined her by treating as hostile witness, no favorable answers has been elicited from her to support the prosecution case that KABC030074402023 CC No.4753/2023 she has deposed falsely to help the accused.

Thus, it emerges from the cross examination of PW1 that the disputes between the accused No. 1 and the PW1 have been settled.

The learned APP argued that the Section 498A R/w Section 34 of Indian Penal code is not compoundable offence as per section 320 of CRPC and hence the examination of witnesses is necessary however this court dispensed the same on account of amicable settlement arrived between the rival parties to the case and PW1 did not support the KABC030074402023 CC No.4753/2023 prosecution case.
Yes this court agrees with the view of the Learned Sr.APP that the section 498A of IPC cannot be compounded as per Section 320 of CRPC.

This court places reliance in the case of B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. STATE OF HARYANA AND ANR IN THE MATTER OF AIR 2003 SCW 1824, wherein it was held that, "in a case where matrimonial disputes have been resolved between the parties then in that case offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. may be compounded between the parties for according to them an opportunity to settle in life afresh.

"It appears that good sense have been prevailed amongst the spouses and when it became impossible for them to lead conjugal life any further and when the matrimonial home has been broken for all practical purposes, they have decided to withdraw all allegations and counter allegations against each other and get KABC030074402023 CC No.4753/2023 themselves separated on divorce by mutual consent.

ADMITTEDLY, the disputes between the PW1 and accused No. 1 have been resolved.
The criminal case under Section 498A of I.P.C. is the off-shoot of the said matrimonial dispute.
The parties have come to their terms and in pursuance thereto the CW1/PW1 does not intend to proceed with this case and hence she has not supported the prosecution case.

18. In the case of the KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464,
wherein it was held that "it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the KABC030074402023 CC No.4753/2023 criminal proceeding or continuation of criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end".

sentences.text: 19. Under these circumstances and on account of the preposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex and Hon'ble High Court, even if other witnesses examined by the prosecution, they did supported the prosecution, would not helpful to the prosecution.
In this background, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.
Moreover the evidence of other witnesses is only formal in nature.

Therefore, the prayer of learned APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and hence the offence under section 498A of IPC with other offences under section 323, 504, 506 of IPC cannot be proved beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, this court answers the point No.1 to 6 in the Negative.

20. Point No.7:- In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1 to 6, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
KABC030074402023 CC No.4753/2023 (i) The accused No.1 to 4 are found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Sec.498(A), 323, 504, 506 Read with Sec.34 of Indian Penal Code and Section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
(ii) Accused are set at liberty.

(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C their bail bonds shall be in force for 6 (six)
months.
